purpose: Defines the canonical domain primitives, token economics, pricing matrix, and intermediate representation (IR) types for the Lumen session intelligence and Prism evaluation platforms.
scope: Covers crates/lumen-model: CanonicalTranscript, CanonicalTurn, ToolIntent, TurnRole, TurnTokenUsage, PricingRate, PricingTable, TokenEconomics, ModelTokenSummary, ExecutionTiming, TrajectoryAnomaly, and SchemaCitation. ModelPricing (the hardcoded per-model match-statement type) is removed from scope this pass, replaced by PricingTable -- see PricingRate/PricingTable's api_surface entry.
non_goals: Log file ingestion, disk I/O, or format parsing (delegated to lumen-session).
Stateful metric accumulation or anomaly detection algorithms (delegated to lumen-analysis and lumen-pattern).
Evaluation assertion grading or test execution (delegated to prism-grader).

Extended-TTL (1-hour) prompt cache pricing for non-Anthropic providers: still true that none publish a selectable 1h-cache rate. STALE CLAIM REMOVED 2026-08-22: this non_goal previously also said TokenEconomics.ephemeral_1h_tokens was 'intentionally unpopulated (hardcoded to 0) pending a future criterion' -- that became false the moment TokenRateKind::CacheWrite1h and TurnTokenUsage.cache_creation_1h_tokens were implemented and wired for Anthropic models (2026-08-21/22, real Claude Code data confirmed to publish the 5m/1h split via usage.cache_creation). The field is populated today for Anthropic; this non_goal now only means 'no 1h tier for the other six providers', not 'no 1h tier at all'.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23 (was previously a planned, not-yet-implemented non_goal -- see CRIT-LUMEN-170): PricingTable::seed() no longer hand-maintains dollar rate literals for every model. It now loads the bulk of its rows from a vendored copy of LiteLLM's community-maintained model_prices_and_context_window.json (crates/lumen-model/data/litellm_model_prices.json, refreshed via `just update-pricing`), filtered to mode:"chat" entries under Lumen's four known adapters' direct first-party providers (anthropic/openai/gemini/vertex_ai-language-models). A small hand-typed layer remains for models that were real and verified at some point but have since rolled off LiteLLM's current snapshot entirely (claude-3-5-sonnet, claude-3-5-haiku, qwen-2.5-coder, claude-opus [v3], deepseek-r1, kimi-k1.5, glm-4-plus, gemini-2.0-pro) -- retained deliberately since Lumen prices historical sessions and a model disappearing from LiteLLM's *current* file must not make real past sessions using it go unpriced. CRIT-LUMEN-002 through 105's literal dollar values for every OTHER model (gpt-4o, gemini-2.0-flash, and all six current-generation models) are now vendored, not hand-typed; the numeric values in those criteria describe the live behavior as verified 2026-08-23, not a hand-maintained source of truth to keep in sync by hand going forward.

api_surface.name: CanonicalTranscript
api_surface.signature: pub struct CanonicalTranscript { pub session_id: CompactString, pub parent_session_id: Option<CompactString>, pub subagent_role: Option<CompactString>, pub orchestrator: OrchestratorKind, pub model_family: CompactString, pub timing: ExecutionTiming, pub economics: TokenEconomics, pub turns: Vec<CanonicalTurn>, pub subagents: Vec<CanonicalTranscript>, pub extracted_schemas: SmallVec<[SchemaCitation; 4]>, pub detected_anomalies: SmallVec<[TrajectoryAnomaly; 4]> }
api_surface.description: Universal normalized transcript representation holding the complete conversation tree, subagent hierarchy, token economics, and extracted schema artifacts. subagent_role (new this pass) is Some(<worker>) for a transcript reached via CanonicalTranscript.subagents, where <worker> is the real path segment from the sibling subagents/<worker>.jsonl filename that produced it (SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION's CRIT-LUMEN-026), and None for a root/non-subagent transcript -- this is the concrete source SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS's by_subagent (CRIT-LUMEN-149) keys on, closing a previously-undefined 'subagent role' reference (audit finding, 2026-08-20). Deliberately NOT a call_id correlation back to the parent's specific ToolIntent::SubagentSpawn invocation -- no real data confirming that correlation is directly available was found this session, so this field only claims what the real sibling-filename convention actually supports.
error_conditions: Deserialization error if JSON payload violates field types

api_surface.name: CanonicalTurn
api_surface.signature: pub struct CanonicalTurn { pub turn_index: usize, pub role: TurnRole, pub timestamp: DateTime<Utc>, pub latency_ms: u64, pub text: Option<String>, pub tool_calls: SmallVec<[CanonicalToolCall; 2]>, pub tool_results: SmallVec<[CanonicalToolResult; 2]>, pub usage: Option<TurnTokenUsage> }
api_surface.description: Normalized user, assistant, system, or tool execution turn.

api_surface.name: ToolIntent
api_surface.signature: pub enum ToolIntent { FileRead { path: CompactString, line_range: Option<(usize, usize)> }, FileEdit { path: CompactString, lines_added: usize, lines_removed: usize }, FileCreate { path: CompactString }, CodeSearch { tool: CompactString, query: CompactString, is_ast: bool }, FileDiscovery { tool: CompactString, pattern: CompactString }, TestExecution { runner: CompactString, target_suite: Option<CompactString> }, VersionControl { action: CompactString }, SubagentSpawn { agent_type: CompactString, description: CompactString }, McpCall { server: CompactString, method: CompactString }, Other { raw_name: CompactString } }
api_surface.description: The closed set of typed tool-call intents every adapter normalizes raw tool invocations into. Named in this spec's scope since its original authoring but never given its own api_surface entry -- CRIT-LUMEN-022 (SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION) and several SPEC-LUMEN-005/006 criteria reference ToolIntent variants with no definition anywhere to bind against (audit finding, 2026-08-20). This entry is the ground truth those criteria bind to.

api_surface.name: PricingRate / PricingTable
api_surface.signature: pub enum TokenRateKind { Input, CacheWrite, CacheRead, Output }; pub struct PricingRate { pub model: CompactString, pub tier: Option<CompactString>, pub kind: TokenRateKind, pub rate_per_m: f64, pub effective_from: DateTime<Utc>, pub effective_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>> }; pub struct PricingTable { pub rates: Vec<PricingRate> }; impl PricingTable { pub fn seed() -> Self; pub fn rate_for(&self, model: &str, tier: Option<&str>, kind: TokenRateKind, as_of: DateTime<Utc>) -> f64; }
api_surface.description: Versioned exchange-rate-style pricing lookup: rate_for selects the PricingRate row for (model, tier, kind) whose [effective_from, effective_until) window contains as_of -- the token-generating turn's own timestamp, never the current wall-clock time -- so historical costs stay correct after a provider changes prices. Replaces the removed ModelPricing hardcoded match statement entirely (ModelPricing is out of scope this pass, see scope); PricingTable::seed() ships the same rate values ModelPricing previously hardcoded, now as dated rows instead of match arms. model matching normalizes raw provider-versioned strings (e.g. "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022") to the seeded canonical keys (e.g. "claude-3-5-sonnet") the same way CRIT-LUMEN-002 through 105's per-provider recognition already requires -- this pass does not change that normalization behavior, only where the resulting rate is looked up. tier is Some("fast")/Some("standard")/etc. for orchestrators reporting a cost-tier signal (e.g. Codex's service_tier, SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION's CRIT-LUMEN-162) and None otherwise; a None-tier row is the default used when the caller has no tier signal to pass. Cross-validated against Langfuse's real Price/PricingTier tables and ccusage's timestamp-gated Kimi pricing cutoff (both real systems, researched 2026-08-20).
error_conditions: IF the requested model string matches no PricingRate row's model field at all (genuinely unrecognized model), THE SYSTEM SHALL fall back to CLAUDE_3_5_SONNET's seeded rate for the requested kind at as_of (CRIT-LUMEN-008).

IF the requested model string DOES match at least one PricingRate row (recognized model) but no row exists for the specific (tier, kind, as_of) combination requested -- e.g. a provider with no seeded CacheWrite rate at all -- THE SYSTEM SHALL return 0.0 for that kind rather than substituting another model's rate (CRIT-LUMEN-161); this is distinct from the unrecognized-model case above.

IF more than one row matches the same (model, tier, kind) with overlapping or identical effective_from windows (an authoring error), THE SYSTEM SHALL select the row with the latest effective_from, and among ties on effective_from, the row appearing LAST in PricingTable.rates' vector order (deterministic, since row declaration order is stable).

api_surface.name: TokenEconomics
api_surface.signature: pub struct TurnPricingInput { pub usage: TurnTokenUsage, pub timestamp: DateTime<Utc>, pub tier: Option<CompactString> }; pub struct TokenEconomics { pub input_tokens: u64, pub output_tokens: u64, pub cache_creation_tokens: u64, pub cache_read_tokens: u64, pub ephemeral_5m_tokens: u64, pub ephemeral_1h_tokens: u64, pub cache_hit_ratio: f32, pub total_cost_usd: f64, pub provided_cost_usd: Option<f64>, pub baseline_cost_no_cache_usd: f64, pub net_savings_usd: f64, pub efficiency_multiplier: f32, pub per_model: HashMap<CompactString, ModelTokenSummary>, pub reasoning_output_tokens: u64, pub is_fully_priced: bool }; impl TokenEconomics { pub fn calculate(turns: &[TurnPricingInput], model_name: &str, pricing: &PricingTable, provided_cost_usd: Option<f64>) -> Self; }
api_surface.description: Aggregated session economics. calculate takes one TurnPricingInput per turn (not pre-summed session totals) and computes total_cost_usd as the SUM of each turn's cost, each priced via PricingTable::rate_for at THAT turn's own timestamp/tier -- required so a session whose turns straddle a price-change boundary (or a Codex service_tier change) is priced correctly on both sides of the boundary, which a single session-level as_of could not represent. input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens on the returned TokenEconomics remain the simple sums across all turns (unaffected by the pricing redesign). provided_cost_usd carries the source's own reported cost (e.g. Claude Code's real costUSD field, confirmed present via ccusage) verbatim alongside the independently computed total_cost_usd, mirroring Langfuse's raw-vs-canonicalized twin-field pattern -- enables drift detection, never used to override total_cost_usd. is_fully_priced (added 2026-08-21, see CRIT-LUMEN-008's rewrite) is false when model_name matched no PricingTable row -- total_cost_usd is still 0.0 in that case (every rate lookup returns 0.0), so this flag is the only signal distinguishing a genuinely free session from an unpriced one; callers MUST check it before treating total_cost_usd as trustworthy. KNOWN GAP (audit finding 2026-08-22, not yet fixed): representing this as a bool sitting next to a float, rather than as a proper sum type (e.g. an enum with Priced(f64)/Unpriced variants), is exactly what let ClaudeCodeAdapter's stale model_family default (claude.rs:37) silently produce a real-looking cost for months without a compiler-enforced check -- a real refactor candidate, not yet done.
error_conditions: Sets cache_hit_ratio to 0.0 and efficiency_multiplier to 1.0 if total prompt tokens is zero
Sets provided_cost_usd to None when the source record carries no provider-reported cost field, never defaulting it to 0.0
An empty turns slice returns a zeroed TokenEconomics (0 cost, 0 tokens), not an error

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN CanonicalTranscript is serialized to JSON and deserialized back to Rust, THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve identical struct equality with zero data loss.
WHEN computing Claude 3.5 Sonnet costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $3.00/M, cache creation writes at $3.75/M (1.25x), cache reads at $0.30/M (0.10x), and output tokens at $15.00/M.
WHEN computing Claude 3.5 Haiku costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $0.80/M, cache creation writes at $1.00/M (1.25x), cache reads at $0.08/M (0.10x), and output tokens at $4.00/M.
WHEN computing Qwen 2.5 Coder costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $0.20/M, cache reads at $0.05/M, and output tokens at $0.60/M.

WHEN computing cache_hit_ratio H, THE SYSTEM SHALL calculate H = (cache_read_tokens / (input_tokens + cache_creation_tokens + cache_read_tokens)) * 100.0 -- H is deliberately stored on a 0-100 percentage scale despite the field's "ratio" name (confirmed matching the real implementation, crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs:45-46), not a 0.0-1.0 fraction.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-20): the field name ("ratio") and the *100.0 formula appeared to contradict each other with no clarifying text. Verified directly against real code that the percentage scale is the actual, deliberate, already-implemented behavior -- the spec text is amended to state this explicitly rather than the formula being changed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN computing financial efficiency multiplier eta, THE SYSTEM SHALL calculate eta = baseline_cost_no_cache_usd / total_cost_usd.
IF total prompt tokens is zero, THE SYSTEM SHALL return cache_hit_ratio of 0.0 and efficiency_multiplier of 1.0 without dividing by zero.

WHEN PricingTable::rate_for is invoked with a model string that matches NO PricingRate row's model field at all (genuinely unrecognized, not merely missing one specific kind -- see CRIT-LUMEN-161 for that distinct case), THE SYSTEM SHALL return 0.0 for every kind (never substitute another model's rate), and PricingTable::is_recognized(model) SHALL return false so callers can distinguish this from a genuinely free session via TokenEconomics::is_fully_priced.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-21 (real-data finding, not the 2026-08-20 audit rewrite below, which this text corrects further): the original 'default to CLAUDE_3_5_SONNET's rate' behavior was found to silently misprice every current real model on a real machine -- claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5, claude-haiku-4-5, claude-fable-5, gpt-5.6-terra, and gemini-3.7-flash all normalized to no seeded row and fell back to stale Sonnet rates, a real, live overcharge/undercharge bug, not a hypothetical. Fixed by removing the substitution entirely in favor of an explicit is_fully_priced=false signal (see TokenEconomics's api_surface entry). The historical rationale below (reconciling this criterion with CRIT-LUMEN-161) still holds for why the two cases are split; only the unrecognized-model resolution changed.
acceptance_criteria.superseded_reasoning_2026_08_20: Rewritten off ModelPricing::from_model_name, which is removed this pass (see scope), onto PricingTable::rate_for -- the single entry point now responsible for all fallback behavior. Audit finding (2026-08-20): the original wording left two independent, potentially-diverging unrecognized-model code paths (this criterion and the new CRIT-LUMEN-161) with no criterion reconciling them; this rewrite plus CRIT-LUMEN-161's narrowing to a distinct case closes that gap by construction -- there is exactly one fallback entry point now, with two clearly distinct trigger conditions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN calculating net USD savings, THE SYSTEM SHALL ensure net_savings_usd is clamped to a minimum of 0.0.
WHEN TurnTokenUsage calculates prompt_tokens, THE SYSTEM SHALL return the sum of input_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, and cache_read_tokens.
WHEN computing Claude Opus costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $15.00/M, cache creation writes at $18.75/M (1.25x), cache reads at $1.50/M (0.10x), and output tokens at $75.00/M.

WHEN computing GPT-4o costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $2.50/M, cache creation writes at $2.50/M (same as the uncached input rate), cache reads at $1.25/M, and output tokens at $10.00/M.

WHEN computing DeepSeek R1 costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $0.55/M, cache creation writes at $0.55/M (same as the uncached input rate), cache reads at $0.14/M, and output tokens at $2.19/M.

WHEN computing Kimi K1.5 costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $0.50/M, cache creation writes at $0.50/M (same as the uncached input rate), cache reads at $0.10/M, and output tokens at $2.00/M.

WHEN computing GLM-4-Plus costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $1.40/M, cache creation writes at $1.40/M (same as the uncached input rate), cache reads at $0.20/M, and output tokens at $1.40/M.

WHEN computing Gemini 2.0 Flash costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $0.10/M, cache creation writes at $0.10/M (same as the uncached input rate), cache reads at $0.025/M, and output tokens at $0.40/M.

WHEN computing Gemini 2.0 Pro costs, THE SYSTEM SHALL bill uncached inputs at $1.25/M, cache creation writes at $1.25/M (same as the uncached input rate), cache reads at $0.30/M, and output tokens at $5.00/M.

WHEN PricingTable::rate_for(model, tier, kind, as_of) is invoked for a RECOGNIZED model (at least one row exists with a matching model field), THE SYSTEM SHALL select the PricingRate row for that (model, tier, kind) whose effective_from is less than or equal to as_of AND whose effective_until is either None or strictly greater than as_of, using the CALLING TURN's own recorded timestamp as as_of -- never the current wall-clock time -- so that a session's cost reflects the rate in effect when the tokens were actually billed, not today's rate. IF more than one row matches with overlapping/identical windows (an authoring error, not a normal case), THE SYSTEM SHALL select the row with the latest effective_from, and among ties on effective_from, the row appearing LAST in PricingTable.rates' declaration order.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Establishes the exchange-rate lookup semantics for the recognized-model case specifically (CRIT-LUMEN-008 and CRIT-LUMEN-161 cover the two distinct unrecognized/missing-kind fallback cases). Audit fixes (2026-08-20): (1) the tie-break was previously incomplete for identical effective_from values -- added a fully deterministic secondary key (vector declaration order); (2) TokenEconomics::calculate now takes per-turn TurnPricingInput (see api_surface) specifically so as_of can be each turn's own timestamp, not one value for an entire multi-turn session that might straddle a price-change boundary -- the prior single-as_of signature could not represent that case correctly regardless of how this criterion was worded, so the API itself was fixed, not just this criterion's text. Design confirmed directly by the user (2026-08-20) using an FX historical-rate-lookup analogy, cross-validated against Langfuse's real Price/PricingTier schema and ccusage's Kimi timestamp-gated pricing cutoff.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IF a raw usage record supplied to TokenEconomics::calculate carries a provider-reported cost value (e.g. Claude Code's real costUSD field), THE SYSTEM SHALL store it verbatim in TokenEconomics.provided_cost_usd; THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT use provided_cost_usd to override, blend with, or short-circuit the independently computed total_cost_usd -- the two fields exist to be compared for drift, not merged.

IF PricingTable::rate_for is invoked for a RECOGNIZED model (at least one row matches the model field) that has no PricingRate row at all for the specific (tier, kind) requested -- e.g. Qwen 2.5 Coder (CRIT-LUMEN-004), which has no seeded CacheWrite rate for any tier or time window -- THE SYSTEM SHALL return 0.0 for that kind, and SHALL NOT substitute CLAUDE_3_5_SONNET's or any other model's rate for it.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-20): the prior wording conflated this case (a real, recognized provider that genuinely never bills for a given token kind) with CRIT-LUMEN-008's genuinely-unrecognized-model case, both falling back to Sonnet's rate -- which would incorrectly apply Anthropic cache-write pricing to a provider (e.g. Qwen) that may not bill cache writes at all. Split into two distinct, independently testable criteria: CRIT-LUMEN-008 (model wholly unrecognized -> Sonnet fallback) and this one (model recognized, this specific kind absent -> 0.0).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23. WHEN PricingTable::seed() is built, THE SYSTEM SHALL source the bulk of its PricingRate rows from a vendored copy of LiteLLM's community-maintained model_prices_and_context_window.json (github.com/BerriAI/litellm, crates/lumen-model/data/litellm_model_prices.json), refreshed via the explicit `just update-pricing` task, NOT from hand-typed Rust literals -- the staleness of hand-typed literals was the direct cause of CRIT-LUMEN-008's real overcharge/undercharge bug (2026-08-21, every current real model on a real machine mispriced). rate_for/normalize_model_key/is_recognized's lookup logic is unaffected -- only seed()'s data source changed, in crates/lumen-model/src/pricing_source.rs's load_vendored_rates. Only "mode": "chat" entries under a direct first-party litellm_provider (anthropic, openai, gemini, vertex_ai-language-models -- the providers Lumen's four known adapters actually draw from; gateway/regional resale listings like bedrock_converse or azure_ai are excluded) are loaded; a pricing field LiteLLM omits produces no row, never an invented value (this corrected two prior hand-typed approximations: gpt-4o and gemini-2.0-flash were assumed to have no separate cache-write charge and priced writes at the input rate, but LiteLLM publishes no cache-write field for either at all, so CacheWrite now correctly returns 0.0 per CRIT-LUMEN-161; gpt-5.6-terra's cache-write rate was assumed equal to its input rate but is actually a real, distinct, higher published rate). A small hand-typed layer remains in PricingTable::seed() for real, previously-verified models that have since rolled off LiteLLM's current snapshot entirely (claude-3-5-sonnet, claude-3-5-haiku, qwen-2.5-coder, claude-opus [v3], deepseek-r1, kimi-k1.5, glm-4-plus, gemini-2.0-pro) -- since Lumen prices historical sessions, a model disappearing from LiteLLM's *current* file must not make real past sessions using it go unpriced. LiteLLM's cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr field was confirmed to match Lumen's 1h-cache-tier need exactly (verified against real Opus 5/Sonnet 5/Haiku 4.5/Fable 5 rates: every field byte-for-byte identical to the prior hand-typed values). Never fetched live: `just update-pricing` is an explicit, reviewed re-vendor step, not a per-request fetch, preserving point-in-time-stable historical pricing.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Research finding (2026-08-22): no viable Rust crate exists for multi-provider LLM pricing (checked llm-pricing, ccost, llm_usages -- all single-maintainer, low-download, narrow-scope). LiteLLM's JSON is the real, actively-maintained answer and was directly cross-validated against rates Lumen hand-seeded this session. Implemented 2026-08-23: the DIRECT_PROVIDERS provider allowlist and the legacy-layer retention decision are both judgment calls made during implementation, not specified in the original criterion -- documented in pricing_source.rs's and PricingTable::seed's doc comments, with an explicit note to revisit the provider allowlist if a future adapter targets a different first-party provider (e.g. a direct DeepSeek, Moonshot, or Mistral API integration).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23. WHEN a cost value is surfaced to a caller that will display or report it, THE SYSTEM SHALL make it structurally difficult to read a dollar figure without also observing whether it is genuinely priced -- via lumen_model::Cost, a sum type (Priced(f64) | Unpriced) obtained from TokenEconomics::cost()/ModelTokenSummary::cost()/lumen_store::SessionSummaryReadModel::cost(), whose Unpriced case must be matched to obtain a number at all. total_cost_usd/is_fully_priced themselves remain the underlying (f64, bool) representation -- required for turn/session cost summation and SQL persistence, both of which need the raw numeric value regardless of pricing status -- Cost is specifically the accessor for the point a cost is surfaced to a human (a CLI table, a report), not a replacement for the stored fields.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit + research finding (2026-08-22): the float-plus-bool representation is exactly what let ClaudeCodeAdapter's stale model_family default (claude.rs:37, a separate confirmed HIGH bug from the same audit) produce a real, silently-wrong cost for an unknown period without any test catching it -- the type system permitted reading total_cost_usd while ignoring is_fully_priced. Research confirmed no external prior art solves this for us (OpenTelemetry's GenAI semantic conventions explicitly leave cost/pricing representation to the consumer entirely) -- this is a Lumen-specific type-modeling decision. Implemented 2026-08-23 as a Cost enum surfaced via .cost() methods rather than replacing the stored (f64, bool) pair everywhere: lumen-store's SQL persistence and lumen-analysis's cross-turn cost summation both genuinely need the raw numeric representation, so the fix targets the actual display/report boundary the criterion's own wording already scoped it to ('at the point cost is surfaced to callers'). Surveying every real total_cost_usd/is_fully_priced call site to apply this (lumen-cli's 3 display sites) surfaced a second, more severe real bug, now tracked separately as SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE.json's CRIT-LUMEN-175: is_fully_priced had no backing column in lumen-store's sessions/token_usage tables at all, so it was silently lost on every store round-trip (hardcoded true on read-back) -- lumen-cli's `sessions` command read total_cost_usd with literally no is_fully_priced check, the exact bug class this criterion exists to make impossible, live in the store layer. Fixed in the same pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FIXED 2026-08-23. WHEN a caller needs a transcript's full economic picture (cmd_ingest's persisted SessionFactRecord.economics, cmd_audit's displayed/JSON economics), THE SYSTEM SHALL include every subagent's cost recursively, via CanonicalTranscript::rolled_up_economics(), NOT CanonicalTranscript.economics alone -- which is built by TokenEconomics::calculate from only the transcript's own turns and silently excludes subagents entirely. rolled_up_economics sums token counts and total_cost_usd/baseline_cost_no_cache_usd across the whole subagent tree, merges per_model entries by model key, recomputes cache_hit_ratio/net_savings_usd/efficiency_multiplier from the rolled totals (they are ratios, not additive), sets is_fully_priced to the AND across the whole tree (one unpriced subagent model makes the combined total just as untrustworthy as an unpriced root), and drops provided_cost_usd (a provider-reported figure that is only ever valid for the single transcript it was attached to -- fabricating a combined one would misattribute it). CanonicalTranscript.economics itself is unchanged and still available for a caller that specifically wants only the root transcript's own turns.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Full-codebase semantic-model review finding (2026-08-23): only ClaudeCodeAdapter ever populates CanonicalTranscript.subagents (via sibling subagents/*.jsonl files); nothing anywhere summed a populated subagents tree's economics into its parent, so cmd_ingest's persisted total_cost_usd and cmd_audit's displayed total both silently under-reported real spend for any session that delegated via subagents, with no field anywhere flagging the number as root-only. Considered but deferred (judgment call): persisting each subagent as its own queryable session row via CanonicalTranscript.parent_session_id (already a populated field, suggesting that may have been the original intent) -- a genuinely larger feature (schema change, new repository/query surface, CLI drill-down UX) with no demonstrated need yet beyond fixing the immediate wrong number; the same no-speculative-infrastructure standing lesson CRIT-LUMEN-174's five deferred repositories were judged against. rolled_up_economics closes the concrete correctness gap (the number is silently wrong) without committing to that larger, unrequested feature; per_model/turn_count/tool_calls attribution across the subagent boundary (which specific subagent spent what) remains future work if a drill-down view is ever requested, consistent with lumen-analysis's existing (currently-unpopulated) AttributionAccumulator being the intended home for that breakdown rather than duplicating it here. Regression tests: test_rolled_up_economics_sums_subagent_cost_into_root, test_rolled_up_economics_is_fully_priced_is_and_of_whole_tree, test_rolled_up_economics_with_no_subagents_matches_own_economics_cost (crates/lumen-model/tests/test_transcript.rs).

reasoning: Establishes the foundational type system, token accounting formulas, and expanded pricing matrices (Sonnet, Haiku, Opus, GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, Gemini) required for downstream analysis.
